honest.title: Faster adoption builds on existing networks
honest.body: ChatGPT reached 100 million people quickly partly because about 5 billion were already online. The telephone needed a copper line to every house. Time to 100 million measures distribution as much as invention.

honest.title: Adoption figures use different yardsticks
honest.body: Subscriptions, accounts, installs and monthly users are not the same thing, and several figures are third-party estimates. Read each line as order-of-magnitude evidence. The table under the chart lists every measure and source.

honest.title: Exponential is not the same as accelerating
honest.body: Transistor counts and solar prices change at a near-constant rate, a straight line on the log scale. That is fast, but the rate is not rising. AI training compute is the clear case where the rate itself rose, from doubling every 20 months to every 6.

honest.title: Recent figures are the least certain
honest.body: Most frontier AI compute values after 2023 are Epoch AI estimates, not disclosures. The newest chips are multi-die packages. NHGRI's genome series ends in 2022. Each data table notes these cases.

honest.title: The milestones are a selection, not a measurement
honest.body: The milestone list is chosen for context, with a source for every entry. Its spacing proves nothing; a different curator would choose differently. The argument rests on the charts.

honest.title: Faster is not the same as bigger
honest.body: Economist Robert Gordon argues that inventions of 1870 to 1970, such as electricity, indoor plumbing, cars and antibiotics, raised living standards on a scale that cannot be repeated, and that growth slowed after 1970. This page measures how fast things spread, not how much they changed daily life.

source.title: The Rise and Fall of American Growth
